direct-proportion.name: Direct proportion
direct-proportion.oneLiner: A relationship where one quantity grows by the same factor as the other
direct-proportion.description: In a direct proportion y = kx, doubling x doubles y and tripling x triples y. The graph is a straight line through the origin, and k is the constant of proportionality.
direct-proportion.significance: It expresses the most basic proportional relationship. As the special case of a linear function whose y-intercept is 0, it is the starting point for all study of proportion.

y.description: The output value determined by x.

k.description: The fixed ratio between x and y. You can find it as k = y/x.

x.description: The input value you are free to choose.

realWorldExamples: The relationship between count and price when one apple costs 500 won
The relationship between time and distance when you travel at a constant speed

inverse-proportion.name: Inverse proportion
inverse-proportion.oneLiner: A relationship where one quantity shrinks by the same factor as the other grows
inverse-proportion.description: In an inverse proportion y = k/x, doubling x halves y and tripling x cuts y to a third. The graph is a hyperbola that comes arbitrarily close to the x- and y-axes without ever touching them.
inverse-proportion.significance: It expresses a relationship that keeps a constant product, and it underpins Boyle's law in physics, the relationship between work and time, and many other phenomena.

y.description: The output value determined by x.

k.description: The value the product of x and y always keeps. You can find it as k = xy.

x.description: The input value, which cannot be 0.

realWorldExamples: Covering the same distance in less time as your speed goes up
In rectangles of equal area, the height shrinks as the width grows

percentage.name: Percentage
percentage.oneLiner: How large a part is when the whole is taken as 100
percentage.description: The percentage p = (part/whole) x 100 expresses what share a quantity takes of the whole on a scale of 100. It uses the percent (%) sign and makes comparison and communication easy.
percentage.significance: It is the most widely used way of expressing a ratio in everyday life — discounts, interest rates, grades, and statistics.

p.description: The ratio taken with the whole as 100. Its unit is %.

부분.description: The size of the part of the whole you want to know about.

전체.description: The whole amount that counts as 100%.

realWorldExamples: The share of questions answered correctly on a test (a score of 80 = 80%)
Working out the actual discount on an item marked 30% off

speed-formula.name: Speed formula
speed-formula.oneLiner: The formula that finds how fast something moves by dividing distance travelled by time taken
speed-formula.description: The speed formula v = d/t gives the distance an object covers per unit of time. It is the most basic formula in physics, tying together the three quantities distance, time, and speed.
speed-formula.significance: It is the most elementary formula for describing motion and the starting point for understanding the distance-time-speed relationship.

v.description: Distance covered per unit of time. For example, 60 km/h means you travel 60 km in one hour.

d.description: The length the object actually travelled.

realWorldExamples: Finding the speed of a car that covers 120 km in 2 hours
Working out an average speed from a 100 m sprint time

density-formula.name: Density formula
density-formula.oneLiner: The formula for how tightly packed a substance is per unit of volume
density-formula.description: The density formula divides mass by volume to find how tightly packed a substance is. At the same size, more mass means higher density; at the same mass, more volume means lower density.
density-formula.significance: It is a basic physical quantity used to tell substances apart and to judge whether something floats or sinks in water.

\\rho.description: Mass per unit volume. The unit is usually g/cm3 or kg/m3.

m.description: The value giving the amount of matter in the object. The unit is g or kg.

V.description: The amount of space the object takes up. The unit is cm3 or m3.

realWorldExamples: Why an iron ball sinks while a wooden block floats
Telling real gold from fake by its density
